title: Suggestions for 4x game workflow and game design learning
author: TheIronAlex
selftext:
Hi everyone, I need some help with my 4x project, I started completely ignorant of game design, mechanics, I'm no coder or graphic artist but I wanted to make a big, (overly) ambitious 4x game like civ, humankind, in 2d, in Claude code.

So far it's been kinda a mess. The graphics looks great (Fable rips) but what's underneath really need a rethink. And an agent won't fix that.

I want to take a step back and stop delegating decisions to ai agents (been recovering from a really bad burn out for months and find decision making really fatiguing), in my ignorance, especially the first month, when I discovered Claude code I thought ai could make great games. They can not. By themselves. I learnt it the hard way.

Especially for something as complicated as 4x games.

It turned in a mess of "answering the mail", doing maths, and really unnecessary concepts.

I don't think I need to restart from 0, however I need some words of advice from some skilled devs.

What could be some useful resources? (For agents but especially for me)

When should I say no to something?

How to stop scope creep?

How can I keep being inspired if I feel so overwhelmed?

How can I judge the core loop when the games isn't finished or doesn't feel as polished as I would like?

Feel free to share your experience as well. I want some human experience sharing, I don't want to ask Claude.
